name: Six of Swords
meaning: The Six of Swords is a symbol of travel, relocation, and moving past difficult times. It represents problems beginning to resolve gradually, letting go of the past, and universal compromise. When merged with Eastern philosophy, this card is the avatar of "The Transition of Yin to Yang" (陰陽 fluctuation). It aligns with the Taoist principle: "Water flows through rocks; all obstacles dissolve when one yields to nature." The number 6 signifies limitless smoothness (Liu Liu Da Shun). The six swords fixed to the bow reflect problems and emotional wounds carried along, but no longer used to hurt anyone. It is a time of steadying oneself to move past the formation of karmic obstacles. However, in this new breeze, Taoist philosophy warns that a journey too smooth may hide long delays, a state of not being 100% free from the shadows of the past, and mental fatigue that still requires time to heal.

core.positive: Crises begin to resolve, life direction changes for the better, safely overcoming obstacles, long-distance travel bringing solutions, and peace gradually recovering.

energy.note: This card grants clearly positive results in ending life's harsh storms. Destiny is moving from darkness into the light. Negative energy only manifests as delays and the need for patience, allowing time to act as the healer.

name: Seven of Swords
meaning:
The Seven of Swords is a symbol of secret plans, tactics, wit, survival, acting behind the scenes, evasion, and the universal danger of deception. When merged with Eastern philosophy, this card is the avatar of "The Shrouded Shadow of Metal Yin - 金陰 Dark Strategy." 
In the Taoist way, this card is like using the power of flowing water and the art of stratagem from ancient military manuals (Zhuge Liang/Sun Tzu), as the teaching says: "War is not just about brute force, but the subtlety within the shadows." The number 7 is the number of tests and intellectual challenges. The seven swords planted before you reflect mental tools and clever tactics. However, within this cunning, Taoist philosophy sternly warns: “He who relies only on trickery to take advantage of Heaven and Earth will ultimately fall to the Law of Karma.”

core.positive: Excellent wit and resourcefulness; out-of-the-box strategies that can solve critical situations instantly; working meticulously behind the scenes; narrowly escaping danger; and reading the enemy's mind in advance.
core.negative: Betrayal, treason, ruthless backstabbing, lack of transparency (grey secrets), all-around scams, unethical actions, and a state of paranoia fearing the truth will be revealed.

energy.note: The primary energy of this card is mysterious, volatile, and ethically toxic (Dark Yin energy controlling the Yang power of the swords). Life proceeds amidst trickery and untrustworthy situations. It is recommended that the seeker use "sharp intellect coupled with morality," avoid anything illegal, and keep their strategies quiet.

oracle.positive: The number 7 signifies formations and the test of truth. The posture of writing a map/manual under the moonlight reflects a "state of Yin accumulating deep intuitive wisdom (accurate subconscious)." The 7 swords planted firmly represent strategic placement, mental weapons, and the clever tactics ready to be used to take the reins of fate and survive enemies.
oracle.negative: The dark night atmosphere and the shadows of the blades reflect "non-transparent actions in the dark," hidden agendas, deep-seated anxiety, and the fear that secrets will leak, leading to stressful overthinking at night.

energy.note: Prominent in high-level wit, but carries accumulated stress from secrecy.

The number 9 is the highest Yang number in Chinese tradition, but when paired with the Suit of Swords (the rigid and sharp Metal element), it transforms into a clashing energy that pierces the inner self. In Taoism, this card reflects an encounter with "Inner Demons" (心魔 - Xin Mo) born from distracted thoughts and ignorance clouding one's vision. Yet, within this agonizing darkness, Taoist philosophy embeds a profound truth: "When Yin reaches its extreme, Yang is born." This mental suffering is a breaking point that forces the seeker to let go of ego and stubbornness to light the lamp of wisdom and dispel the shadows of illusion.

When merged with Eastern philosophy, this card is the avatar of "Yin reaching its extreme to give birth to Yang" (陰極生陽). In the Taoist path, it corresponds to "Wuji" (無極 - the original emptiness before the universe began), following the teaching: "When something reaches its limit, it must return to its origin." The number 10 (十) signifies the permanent end of an old cycle. The ten swords surrounding the warrior reflect the "death of the Ego and the illusion of ignorance" shattered by truth. Though this "life reset" brings deep pain, from a Taoist perspective, it is the mercy of Heaven and Earth forcing the seeker to abandon rotting ruins to prepare for the light of a new dawn shining from the mountain peak.

name: Page of Swords
meaning: Universally, the Page of Swords represents the 'Air element in its initial phase,' signifying alertness, developing intellect, surveillance, information, and vigilance. When merged with Taoist philosophy, this card embodies 'initial Yang energy hidden within the silence of Yin.' It reflects a state of sharp mental clarity, observing the world's changes without rushing—much like the Taoist teaching of using stillness to perceive the truth. However, it remains a youthful energy that can become overly anxious or paranoid if not balanced.

core.positive: During this period, you will be highly alert and well-aware of your surroundings. Your mind is clear, curious, and ready to learn new things. It is an excellent time for research, seeking the truth, or protecting your rights. You are living life with prudence and care.
core.negative: Excessive Air energy may turn you into someone who is 'anxious, depressed, and paranoid of those around you.' Your mind is easily shaken by rumors or the words of others, like someone jumping at shadows out of fear of a threat that hasn't arrived. You lack the true stillness of the Tao.

oracle.description: Represents the 'external world full of movement and chaos.' The light from the lanterns reflects active Yang energy, while he watches from the shadows, representing Yin energy.

oracle.description: The moon is the ultimate Yin energy, signifying intuition, premonitions, and secrets about to be revealed. The tall tower is a symbol of boundaries and protection.

oracle.description: Represents the Air element (thoughts, communication, news) that is carrying changes or important information to the seeker.

name: Knight of Swords
meaning: Universally, the Knight of Swords represents the "Fire of Air" (the element of Air in its active phase), signifying speed, agility, sharp intellect, logic, charging fearlessly toward goals, and confronting challenges. When integrated with Taoist philosophy, this card embodies "Extreme Yang energy surging forward," symbolizing a powerful, reckless whirlwind filled with strong will. The dual swords in hand represent proactive wisdom used to cut through cycles of failure, clearing obstacles to pave a new path (Tao). However, it may lack the Yin balance that provides slowness and prudence.

core.positive: Life at this time is driven by high speed, alertness, and sharp intellectual creativity. The brain works as fast as a lightning strike. You are courageous enough to face the truth, charge at your goals, and quickly resolve long-standing, lingering problems.
core.negative: Excessive Yang energy without the restraint of Yin will make you impatient, impulsive, and hot-tempered. You may become self-centered, striving to win while lacking empathy for those around you. Living life in such a rush may lead to mistakes or accidents caused by negligence.

name: Ace of Wands
meaning: The Ace of Wands, or the 1 of Wands, is a universal symbol of new beginnings in ambition, career, projects, creativity, vitality, and proactive drive. When merged with Eastern philosophy, this card represents the 'Inception of Wood and Fire Yang' (木火陽始). It aligns with the Taoist principle that 'Heaven and Earth generate Yang energy for movement and growth.' The wand is a branch (Wood element) ready to serve as fuel to spark a flame (Fire element), granting wisdom, alertness, and enthusiasm. However, amidst this heat, Taoist philosophy warns that a fire raging too quickly (overflowing Yang) can turn into impatience, recklessness, haste, and a state of 'self-combustion' (Burnout), leading to collapse before a solid foundation can be built.

core.positive: The start of a new project, a surge in creativity, fully awakened Qi energy, ambition leading to success, powerful inspiration, and golden career opportunities.
core.negative: Impulsiveness, overextending oneself, acute burnout, rushing while overlooking details, and an ego that seeks to overcome obstacles through sheer force.

energy.note: This card bestows energy, progress, and victory in initiating plans. The negative aspect serves only as a reminder to control haste and prevent the mind from becoming scattered.

The sacred staff is the 'Pillar of Determination,' indicating that the seeker's destiny has received a divine decree and the creativity needed to transform their professional status into something great.
oracle.negative: The solemn atmosphere and the erupting fire warn of new pressures and burdens to be carried—great responsibilities as the spearhead of a task that requires high physical and mental energy.

energy.note: Outstanding in terms of charisma, talent, and intellectual alertness in work.

oracle.symbol: A magical Golden Dragon (Long) dancing, breathing sparks of fire and swirling in an infinite circle above a celestial gourd.

oracle.negative: The Fire Dragon's energy is highly aggressive and hot. If the seeker lacks mindfulness, ego and anger can easily incinerate the allies around them, leading to ruin.

energy.note: Guarantees a great victory and support from sacred powers associated with authority and prestige.

name: Two of Wands
meaning: The Two of Wands is a symbol of future planning, broad vision, territorial expansion, waiting for the right timing, and being a commander who holds a strategic advantage on a global scale. When merged with Eastern philosophy, this card is the avatar of the "state of accumulating Yin to drive proactive Yang" (Strategic Yang Preparation - 陰陽 Strategic Planning). In Taoism, this card represents the Wood and Fire elements in a state of preparation, echoing the teachings: "A journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step" and "A visionary plans before the sky turns dark." The young warrior standing with his back turned, looking at a map and gazing toward the mountains, signifies an intellect that refuses to be confined by old boundaries. However, within this prudence and vision, Taoist philosophy warns that an excess of Yang energy—thinking about expansion without taking action (over-contemplation)—can lead to becoming mired in unreachable ambitions, indecisiveness, and standing lonely atop a tower of power without true friends by one's side.

core.positive: Sharp vision, precise strategic planning, opportunities for business expansion or overseas investment, receiving honor and fame, stability in one's stronghold, and controlling the timing of 'Heaven's Opening' for progress.
core.negative: Hesitation to leave the safe zone to face the world, ambitions that exceed reality, a state of isolation with no one to consult ("cold at the top"), and being stuck in the planning phase until work is delayed.

energy.note: This card grants leadership, charisma, and the correct vision for managing life. The negative aspect is merely a reminder not to dwell in static thoughts for too long, lest you lose the driving energy of action.

oracle.symbol: A young warrior with flowing hair, back turned, holding a map on the balcony of an ancient Chinese pavilion tower, gazing across forests and mountains toward the rising sun, with the Chinese number 「二」 (2) above.

The posture of turning the back while holding a map and watching the sunrise signifies "receiving the Mandate of Heaven and calmly assessing the situation according to the Yin way." The robes fluttering in the breeze represent flexibility and the readiness to adapt to the direction of auspicious winds.
oracle.negative: The silhouette standing alone on high ground warns of "isolation," deep-seated anxiety regarding the responsibility of a large plan, or being trapped within mental walls, refusing to step out of the safe zone of one's own tower.

energy.note: Promotes charisma, strategic victory, and far-reaching wisdom.

oracle.negative: A reminder that if one intends to expand the foundation in all four directions, the seeker must possess responsibility and discipline as solid as rock. One must not be fickle or make decisions based on emotion, as this will cause the original family foundation to shake.

name: Three of Wands
meaning: The Three of Wands is a symbol of foresight, project progress, business expansion, international trade, and the anticipation of returns that are on their way. When merged with Eastern philosophy, this card represents the state of 'Flourishing Wood-Fire Yang' (木火大陽). It aligns with the Taoist principle that 'when the foundation is firm (from the Two of Wands), the branches will naturally spread out to receive the sunlight.' The number 3 is the point of conception for all things in the physical world, reflecting the union of Heaven (timing), Earth (location/opportunity), and Man (effort), creating a flow of prosperity. However, within this prosperity, Taoist philosophy warns to be careful: over-ambition or expanding too quickly (excessive Yang) can lead to carelessness, neglecting the 'back house' (internal affairs), or focusing so much on distant goals that one overlooks silent dangers beneath their feet.

core.positive: Broad and accurate vision, clear progress of work invested in, golden opportunities for market expansion or international contact, supportive partners, and the anticipation of beautiful success.

name: Four of Wands
meaning: The Four of Wands is a symbol of stability, sustainable success, celebration, homecoming, and the establishment of a solid life foundation. When merged with Eastern philosophy, this card is the avatar of the 'State of Unified Yin-Yang for a Permanent Foundation' (Consolidated Wood-Fire Yang - 木火 Solid Foundation), aligning with Taoist principles that emphasize balance and sustainability. The number 4 represents the four pillars supporting the universe (the four directions/four seasons) in perfect harmony. It is the point where the proactive Yang energy of work (Wands/Wood element) and honor/fame (Fire element) is transformed into physical structures, security, and peaceful happiness in the material world. However, within this perfection and abundance, Taoist philosophy warns that a state of peak success—if one becomes reckless or lost in the 'mask' of fame (excessive Yang suppressing the Yin of solitude)—can lead to negligence, stagnation, or the creation of rigid traditional frameworks that stifle spiritual freedom.

core.positive: Permanent stability in life, widespread honor and reputation, major auspicious events and celebrations, laying a secure foundation for business or family, and receiving high social recognition.
core.negative: Attachment to social masks and status (success ego), complacency leading to a halt in self-development, rigid traditions that cause suffocation, and anxiety stemming from family expectations.

energy.note: This is one of the most auspicious and favorable cards in the Minor Arcana. It bestows prosperity, safety, and peace upon one's destiny. The negative aspect serves only as a reminder not to get lost in vanity.

oracle.symbol: A young warrior or scholar in white robes with blue trim, standing gracefully on the balcony of an ancient Chinese pavilion, admiring success amidst four dragon-carved wands planted firmly in a row, with the Chinese numeral 「四」 (4) prominent above.
oracle.positive: The number 4 signifies a structural foundation that will never collapse. The young scholar in white reflects pure and elegant wisdom. Standing calmly while viewing the landscape signifies a state where the mind has achieved its goals and escaped the storms of past hard labor.
oracle.negative: The back and the overly still posture warn of a 'safe zone stagnation'—being so satisfied with what one has that the Yang drive to pioneer new things is lost.

energy.note: Promotes charisma, rank, title, and the successful establishment of life's foundation.

oracle.symbol: A pair of white silk battle banners flanking the back, inscribed with large auspicious Chinese calligraphy: on the left 「光耀門楣」 (Guāngyào ménméi) and on the right 「去錦還鄉」 (Qùjǐn huánxiāng).
oracle.positive: The highest decree of honor. The left side translates to 'Bringing light and glory to the family name.' The right side translates to 'Returning to the homeland in silken robes (returning home wealthy and successful).' This confirms the seeker's destiny is ready for fame, highest promotion, or a flourishing family business, bringing pride to the lineage.
oracle.negative: The heavy framework of honor and social face forces the seeker to maintain a perfect image at all times, hiding a deep, accumulated stress.

energy.note: Supports honor, power, fortune, and receiving the highest level of social recognition.

oracle.symbol: Four sacred wands carved with ancient golden dragon patterns, planted firmly on the right side.
oracle.positive: Four wands planted in parallel are as strong as the pillars supporting a kingdom (abundant Wood element). The dragon (Long) is a symbol of Yang power, prestige, and protective sacred entities guarding one's destiny, ensuring peace and safety from enemies.
oracle.negative: The density of the wands warns that the current life structure may be too rigid and overly focused on rules, lacking flexibility and flow.

energy.note: Provides maximum security for assets, business, and the management of subordinates.

oracle.symbol: A background of mountain valleys, auspicious mist, complex Chinese palaces, and white flowers blooming clearly at the bottom.
oracle.positive: Millionaire-level Feng Shui (facing the prosperity of the capital, backed by mountains). White flowers (pure Metal element) signify untainted happiness. The environment nurtures a destiny of abundance and cool peace.
oracle.negative: The grandeur and luxury of the environment hide a subtle anxiety from the expectations of a society that is constantly watching you.

energy.note: Excellent environment for attracting wealth; assets remain stable for a long time.

name: Five of Wands
meaning: The Five of Wands is a symbol of competition, conflict, chaos, disagreement, differing attitudes, and universal struggle. When merged with Eastern philosophy, this card represents a state of "Uncontrolled Active Yang of Wood and Fire elements exploding in all directions" (Uncontrolled Active Yang - 木火 Chaos). It aligns with Taoist principles that warn: "When one allows ego and restlessness to take over, the mind becomes disordered and turbulent." The number 5 is the number of volatility and the clash of the Five Elements. The 5 wands in the image do not signify lethal combat, but rather "martial arts sparring to test and refine potential." Yet, within this chaos, Taoist philosophy views conflict as a driving force for reorganization. If this scattered energy can be channeled creatively, it will bring rapid progress and a soaring ascent.

core.positive: Alert energy driving new creativity, brainstorming, competition that develops professional skills, victory achieved through overcoming obstacles, and learning to adapt amidst chaos.
core.negative: Difficult-to-pin-down chaos, verbal arguments and clashes, conflict within groups or organizations, impulsiveness, and a state of "self-burning" (Burnout) until the body's Qi loses balance.

energy.note: The primary energy of this card is quite restless, urgent, and headache-inducing (led by erupting hot Yang). Life proceeds exhaustingly with constant immediate problems to solve. The reminder is to control your emotions and use the way of "still water" to subdue the chaos.

oracle.symbol: 5 young warriors in various ancient outfits (white, blue, purple, brown, white armor) holding staffs or wands in sparring stances, clashing frantically, with the Chinese numeral 「五」 (5) prominent at the top.
oracle.positive: The number 5 reflects the Five Elements (Earth, Water, Fire, Wood, Metal) clashing and shifting to find a new balance. The diverse colors of the outfits reflect differing visions, thoughts, and ideas, which, if merged, will create great innovation. The active poses reflect vibrant life energy that refuses to surrender to obstacles.
oracle.negative: The tangled mess of wands reflects "disordered chaos and team politics." Each side has a high ego and desires to win with their own ideas, risking communication breakdowns and wasting energy on useless verbal clashes.

energy.note: Indicates a chaotic environment that requires high wit to organize.

oracle.symbol: Red leaves (maple/autumn leaves) scattered across the ground below.
oracle.positive: A symbol of the season of change and shedding the old (natural Yin energy). It reminds the seeker that the current chaos is temporary, waiting for the day of entering peace and coolness.
oracle.negative: Falling leaves reflect the fragments of damage or the exhaustion occurring during the struggle. Emotions as hot as a forest fire consume inner warmth.

energy.note: Must beware of danger from impulsiveness and sharp words that slip out and hurt feelings.

oracle.symbol: Background of an ancient pine tree on the left, steep mountains, mist, and a Chinese pavilion palace on a cliff top with a waterfall.
oracle.positive: The pine tree (Song) signifies endurance, toughness, resilience, and stability amidst storms. The pavilion on the high mountain guides the destiny to see the ultimate goal that remains safe. The waterfall's Feng Shui helps cool the heat of fire energy in the brain.
oracle.negative: Steep mountains and thick mist reflect a life path where karmic obstacles are hidden in every direction. A dilemma where one must primarily rely on oneself to break through the formations of malicious people.

energy.note: Excellent environment for training and sharpening wisdom, but do not ignore warning signs around you.

Being in a competitive situation will push you to develop skills rapidly. Using logic, reason, and mindfulness to organize your life will allow you to pass through this trial gracefully.
* Negative: Life proceeds with dizzying chaos (whatever you do, small obstacles constantly interrupt). You are surrounded by people causing headaches. Beware of impulsiveness, letting anger erupt into words that destroy surrounding friendships.
* ⚖️ Energy Weight: Positive 40% / Negative 60%. Life is active and bustling but exhaustingly tiring. Adhere to the principle of "stillness and keeping the mouth shut." Avoid arguments with others and focus on performing your own duties to the best of your ability.

Fluctuating company policies that change morning and evening make work difficult. Beware of backstabbing and attempts to undermine your position.

* Negative: Love loses its sweet romance, turning into emotional pride and sarcasm to win over each other constantly (sulking over small things, daily arguments). Beware of stress from trying to control or frame the other's life too much, causing suffocation.

* Negative: Encountering a sudden "train wreck" relationship or falling for someone who flirts superficially (becoming just one of their options). Stuck in a vague, competitive love triangle that exhausts the heart.

When the Five of Wands is reversed, the 5 wands fall from the hands. The warriors retreat and go their separate ways. The red leaves stop falling. The chaotic Yang energy suddenly extinguishes and dissipates:

You have awakened, dissolved your ego and pride, and agreed to take one step back to find a partner or good friend. Plans return to a peaceful, orderly system following the correct Middle Way.

Conflicts are swept under the rug, accumulating negative energy ready to explode more violently later. Accounts are chaotic and delayed.
* ⚖️ Energy Weight: Positive 70% / Negative 30%. Energy flips to a clearly positive peak in terms of escaping the swamp of headaches. Peace and coolness return to life. The soul awakens, ready to start reorganizing destiny with enthusiasm and strength.

name: Six of Wands
meaning: The Six of Wands is a symbol of victory and success after a long struggle. it represents receiving public recognition, fame, honor, and widespread popularity. When integrated with Eastern philosophy, this card is the avatar of 'Triumphant Yang Ascension' (木火通明), aligning with Taoist and Bazi principles where the Wood element (Wands/Perseverance) perfectly generates the Fire element (Light/Fame). The number 6 is a highly auspicious number representing supreme smoothness and expanding fortune (Liu Liu Da Shun). it signifies the union of Heaven (opening of destiny), Earth (recognized foundation), and Man (endurance and courage). However, within this elegant luxury, Taoist philosophy warns that 'the prominent tree is the first to be shaken by the wind.' Brilliant success, if accompanied by indulgence or an inflated ego (excessive Yang suppressing the Yin of humility), will create silent enemies in the shadows or lead to a fall from the horse due to complacency.

core.positive: Decisive victory, widespread fame and honor, winning competitions or auctions with legitimacy, a clear upward trajectory in life, and having a circle of followers who admire and believe in you.
core.negative: Ego and self-delusion, attachment to temporary praise, being targeted by jealousy and backstabbing, and complacency that leads to neglecting continuous self-development.

energy.note: This card is highly auspicious, bestowing powerful blessings of success and fame. The negative energy serves as a reminder to maintain humility according to the Middle Way, preventing ego from destroying one's life Feng Shui in the long run.

oracle.symbol: A young warrior in white and gold robes riding a fine white horse, waving gracefully. He is surrounded by a troop of soldiers raising 6 sacred dragon-carved wands, with the Chinese numeral 「六」 (6) prominent at the top.
oracle.positive: The number 6 signifies smoothness without obstacles. The general on the white horse (Bai Ma) is a symbol of pure Yang energy, victory, elegance, and leadership that commands success. Standing above others on horseback represents 'a destiny reaching its peak with prominent honor.' The surrounding followers signify charisma and unanimous acceptance from the collective.
oracle.negative: Standing prominently in the spotlight warns of the 'perils of prominence.' The tallest tree in the forest is shaken by the wind first. There is a risk of being scrutinized by jealous people in the shadows or creating enemies unknowingly through boastful behavior.

energy.note: Promotes prestige, rank, and the successful achievement of victory in competitions.

oracle.symbol: An ancient Chinese palace gate decorated with auspicious red silk and engraved with golden Chinese characters 「金榜題名」 (Jīnbǎng tímíng).
oracle.positive: A divine decree granting great fortune, meaning 'ranking at the top and having one's name engraved on the Emperor's Golden Board (the ultimate success).' The red and gold colors (Fire and Metal elements) dispel all misfortune, bringing good news, fame, and wealth flowing legitimately into the family treasury.
oracle.negative: A reminder that titles and worldly rewards are temporary. Carrying the weight of a great family name brings social pressure and constraints that can make it difficult to live freely according to the natural Tao.

energy.note: Guarantees success in interviews, further education, and reaching the highest levels of promotion.

oracle.symbol: 6 ancient golden dragon-carved sacred wands tied with red ribbons fluttering in the wind.
oracle.positive: The six wands held upright and firm signify 'strength, subordinates, and a foundation of work as solid as the Wood element.' The Dragon (Long) pattern is a symbol of great power and sacred beings acting as guardians to keep one's destiny safe.
oracle.negative: The fluttering red ribbons warn that the currents of fame and public popularity are as volatile as the wind. One must not become attached or intoxicated by them.

energy.note: Provides maximum security in business and ensures subordinates are obedient and under control.

oracle.symbol: A background of complex mountain ranges, auspicious mist, and a long flowing waterfall.
oracle.positive: Imperial-level Feng Shui (facing the capital's gate of prosperity, backed by stable mountains). The water represents profit and assets flowing continuously to fulfill life. The surrounding environment is safe and supportive of one's destiny.
oracle.negative: The steepness of the mountains warns that this great success was earned through long-term toil in the past; wisdom must be used to maintain this stability.

energy.note: The environment supports a destiny of sustainable abundance and happiness.

general:
* Positive: Hearty congratulations! The time for 'celebrating victory and public recognition' has arrived in your life. What you have toiled for and endured in the past is now bearing beautiful fruit, making you the center of social attention. Your wisdom and wit are sharp. Living according to the principle of humility and taking a step back in the Middle Way will expand your prestige without attracting enemies.
* Negative: Beware of 'intoxication with praise' leading to an ego that suppresses others. Acting like a dictatorial emperor may cause those around you to become jealous and gossip behind your back. Complacency might also cause you to let your success stagnate.
* ⚖️ Energy Weight: Positive 85% / Negative 15%. Your destiny is on a clear upward trend. Problems and obstacles will be crushed by your own prestige and ability. Just maintain your mindfulness and humility, and you will be free from danger.
finance:
* Positive: Financial prospects are excellent and flourishing. There is a chance of receiving a large sum of money from rewards, bonuses, or investment returns from the past flowing into your treasury. The Seven of Wands is a symbol of defending one's position, standing firm to protect interests, and maintaining a strategic geographical advantage. It represents handling pressure and achieving victory over obstacles and competitors from all directions. When merged with Eastern philosophy, this card is the avatar of 'Resolute and Aggressive Yang Energy standing firm to suppress the surrounding challenging Yin forces' (Defensive Yang Sovereignty - Wood and Fire holding the high ground). This aligns with Taoist principles and the art of war: 'When one commands the high ground, they can easily suppress those with ill intent below.'

The number 7 is the number of trials and professional elevation. The seven wands reflect will, knowledge, and duty. However, within this resolute strength, Taoist philosophy warns of 'accumulated fatigue' and an ego that is too rigid to compromise (excessive Yang tension suppressing gentle Yin), which can create mental blockages if one does not find time to rest.

The Eight of Wands is a symbol of speed, leapfrog progress, long-distance communication, sudden good news, air travel, and situations moving forward rapidly on a global scale. When merged with Eastern philosophy, this card is the avatar of "High-Speed Active Yang of the Wood and Fire elements soaring to break through stagnation" (High-Speed Active Yang - 木火疾 soaring). It aligns with the Taoist principle: "When the auspicious wind blows, all things move fluidly and change instantly."
The number 8 in both international and Eastern traditions is the number of infinite energy (Infinity) and flowing, circulating wealth. The eight wands carved and soaring in parallel directions represent pure and powerful "Qi" energy, free from obstacles. However, within this speed, Taoist philosophy warns against the negative aspect of "reckless haste," the lack of Yin energy to act as a brake, which can lead to volatile carelessness and a state of "spinning with the current" if one lacks a grounded foundation of mindfulness.

name: Nine of Wands
meaning:
The Nine of Wands is a symbol of standing firm at the final hurdle, accumulated exhaustion, and constant vigilance. It represents a dilemma near the finish line and preparing to face a new wave of obstacles. In international terms, when merged with Eastern philosophy, this card represents a state of "Defensive Yang Exhaustion"—where Yang energy has been pushed to its limit, forcing one into a Yin mode for self-preservation.

The number 9 is the peak of Yang energy, as taught in the I Ching and Taoist philosophy: "When Yang reaches its zenith, it is inherently accompanied by exhaustion, like a dragon weary from its cultivation." The nine wands are arranged as a defensive fortress, indicating that the seeker has endured heavy battles until their body and mind are deeply fatigued, yet they cannot retreat. However, within this weariness, the Tao hides a positive truth: this final endurance is the forge that creates a true master. If you can push through this friction, permanent victory will immediately manifest.

core.positive: An iron will that refuses defeat; establishing a solid self-defense system; great endurance against high-pressure environments; the wit to maintain a defensive stance to subdue troublemakers; and being very close to achieving a major goal.
core.negative: A state of critical accumulated exhaustion (chronic tension); paranoia and irrational fear; silent stubbornness and refusing to accept help; oppressive workloads; and stagnant or sluggish Qi flow.

energy.note: The energy of this card is highly tense and heavy (exhausted Yang pulling on Yin for support). Life proceeds amidst high-pressure situations. Good fortune will arise when you learn to "be still and stay cool," refusing to engage in conflict with impulsive emotions.

oracle.symbol: A young warrior in a white robe with grey trim, leaning back to rest wearily on stone stairs in front of a Chinese pavilion. name: Ten of Wands
meaning:
The Ten of Wands is a universal symbol of carrying a heavy burden, overwhelming responsibility, and the exhaustion of struggling until one's limits are reached. It represents the intense pressure felt just before achieving a ultimate goal. When merged with Eastern philosophy, this card is the avatar of the "Peak of Yang Burden" (陽極)—a state where the Yang energy of perseverance rages beyond physical limits until it weighs heavily upon the soul.

In Chinese tradition, the number 10 (十) signifies completion, fulfillment, and perfection. However, within the suit of Wands (Wood and Fire elements), it reflects that the seeker has reached the final stage of building their life, carrying the weight of the family business (Gongsi) or their own dreams entirely on their back. This aligns with Confucian teachings on resolute duty and responsibility. Yet, Taoism warns of a fundamental truth: "That which is stretched too tight will snap; that which is carried beyond one's strength destroys the balance of Life Qi." Without knowing when to let go and cultivate Yin (calmness), the fire of ambition will burn the self out before reaching the mountain peak.

core.positive: Admirable endurance and grit; great and reliable responsibility; a work structure nearing successful completion; unwavering determination against fate; and being entrusted with high-level policy or significant missions.
core.negative: Severe Burnout Syndrome; accumulated stress and nervous tension; workaholism that destroys life balance; neglecting the joy around oneself; and carrying the burdens of others to the point of personal suffering.

energy.note: This card emphasizes exhaustion, pressure, and overwhelming physical obstacles (excessive Yang consuming the mind). The positive side is the guarantee that "what you are doing is nearly finished and the rewards will be worth it." The key lesson is learning to delegate and follow the Middle Way.

oracle.symbol: A young warrior in tattered, dull clothing, walking with a hunched back, carrying a wicker basket containing 10 dragon-carved wands on his shoulders. He trudges through a steep, rocky path, while three figures of different ages (an elder, a woman, and a child) watch supportively from behind. The Chinese numeral 「十」 (10) is prominent at the top center.
oracle.positive: The number 10 signifies the end of toil to welcome success. The act of moving forward relentlessly reflects the "Yang power of an iron will." The 10 dragon-carved wands represent an honorable mission, a noble title, or the wealth of the family estate he is carrying toward the dream. The three figures behind represent the family who are his inspiration and are waiting to share in the fruits of success.
oracle.negative: The hunched figure and tattered clothes reflect a "deep physical crisis of exhaustion." He carries a burden that is too tight and heavy for his frame. The steep path ahead indicates accumulated mental stress and anxiety so great that he cannot see the beauty surrounding him.

energy.note: Clearly shows supreme responsibility, but the internal state is strained to the breaking point.

oracle.symbol: 10 ancient golden dragon-carved sacred wands packed tightly in a woven basket tied with red ribbons.
oracle.positive: The upright, tightly packed wands represent "power, assets, and completed plans as solid as the Wood element." The Dragon (Long) pattern paired with red ribbons (Fire element) signifies honor, fame, and the authority the seeker holds firmly. The work system is secure and robust.
oracle.negative: The weight pressing down on the shoulders warns of "carrying work, debt, or the problems of others" (an inability to say no). The further one goes, the more exhausted they become, leading to blocked Qi circulation.

energy.note: Guarantees that the results are substantial and grand, but they must be exchanged for immense time and sweat.

oracle.symbol: A background of steep mountain ranges, thick mist, an ancient Chinese pavilion on the left cliff, and a long waterfall flowing down on the right.
oracle.positive: The Feng Shui of the waterfall helps wash away the heat of the Fire element in the brain. The Chinese pavilion on the cliff peak is the ultimate goal of success and a permanent safe zone (strong Earth element) waiting to welcome you upon arrival.
oracle.negative: The steep cliffs and thick fog reflect a life vision that remains blurred and a path surrounded by oppressive karma. One must rely primarily on their own endurance as there is no one else to help carry the load.

energy.note: The natural landscape provides protection from evil, but the path is difficult and emotionally taxing.

The problems you face will be resolved through your own ability and endurance. This is a good time for clearing large projects; living according to the path of perseverance and filial piety will keep you safe from all obstacles.
* Negative: Life is stuck in a pit of exhaustion, chaos, and turmoil. You are surrounded by headaches, carrying the world and its burdens until your back bends. Beware of rushing yourself into a state of chronic stress, muscle tension, or letting your ego and ambition trap you in a way that robs you of the happiness found in the Middle Way.
* ⚖️ Energy Weight: Positive 40% / Negative 60%. Life is active and bustling but exhausting to the core. Adhere to the principle of "yielding and balancing." Let go of small matters and delegate work to subordinates to survive with grace.

* Negative: A state of tension and stress regarding heavy debts or fixed expenses (money comes in and immediately goes out to sustain the family system). There is absolutely no windfall or luck from gambling. Expenses surge from caring for subordinates and relatives that you cannot refuse.

When the Ten of Wands is reversed, the ancient stone stairs shift direction, the wicker basket tips over, and all 10 golden dragon wands scatter and fall from the shoulders. The young warrior looks up, wipes his sweat, and straightens his back. The rising sun shines brightly. The obsessive Yang energy of workaholism collapses, dissolves, or suddenly flips its pole:

You have the courage to dump toxic missions, refuse to be exploited, successfully delegate work to others, and return to a simple, solitary life—loving yourself and relaxing in the bright new Middle Way.
* Negative: The team system collapses suddenly (Qi exhaustion / giving up on obstacles abruptly / abandoning work and fleeing problems, shocking the organization). Sudden termination of contracts. Serious damage to confidential work systems due to negligence and impulsiveness. Subordinates become rebellious, betraying or tearing up family business contracts. Legal cases fall into a critical disadvantage. Severe liquidity crisis in finances. Loss of professional credibility.
* ⚖️ Energy Weight: Positive 70% / Negative 30%. The energy flips to a clear positive in terms of "releasing and unlocking life's knots and breaking down the walls of work-related stress." The pressure dissolves. Wisdom and health return to full power, ready to move forward and reorganize your destiny with enthusiasm.

name: Page of Wands
meaning: In universal terms, the Page of Wands represents the "Fire element in its beginning phase," signifying new inspiration, enthusiasm, news of new projects, discovery, and a desire to learn challenging things. When integrated with Taoist philosophy, this card embodies a "Yang spark just beginning to ignite amidst Yin stillness and contemplation," aligning with the path of intellectual rooting before expanding energy. It is a card of curiosity—the spirit of a seeker tracing the secrets of the universe to create a new Path (Tao) for life.

core.negative: If the fire energy lacks patience, you may become someone who "gets bored easily or has short-lived enthusiasm (straw fire)." You might have many ideas but never finish any (reading many books but never applying them), or you may be so excited and expectant that your mind becomes restless, lacking the stillness of the Tao.

name: Knight of Wands
meaning: Internationally, the Knight of Wands represents the "Air of Fire" (the most active phase of the Fire element). It signifies ambition, inspiration, courage, adventure, and the enthusiastic start of new projects. When merged with Taoist philosophy, this card embodies "Yang energy erupting to drive change," like a spark that ignites and is ready to spread and expand its territory. It aligns with the Taoist teaching of the powerful circulation of life energy (Qi), symbolizing moving forward with internal drive. However, one must be careful not to let the thirst for success burn away the Yin balance that provides coolness and sustainability.

core.positive: Life during this period is full of color. Your life energy is surging, and you are filled with courage and readiness to face any challenge. You will feel alert and ready to explore the wide world, travel far, relocate, or start something new you are 100% passionate about. The mind is filled with hope and enthusiasm.
core.negative: If mindfulness fails to pull the reins, your enthusiasm can turn into impatience and recklessness, acting like a "straw fire" (starting grandly but quitting quickly). A love for challenge may become carelessness, overlooking the detailed Yin prudence, which may lead to mistakes along the way.

This signifies "proactive power, well-prepared project structures, and driving large-scale goals at high speed."

oracle.symbol: Complex mountain ranges and swirling dust clouds behind
oracle.description: The tough stone mountains are physical obstacles waiting to be crossed. The scattered dust reflects "speed, bustle, and a dynamic life situation." Everything around is full of excitement and alertness.

oracle.symbol: Faint light breaking through the cloud curtain above
oracle.description: The rising sun points to the dawn of opportunity and success that aligns with the Way of Nature (Tao).

general:
Card Weight: Dominantly Positive 75% / Negative 25%
* Positive Perspective (Yang erupting to drive creativity): Life during this period is full of color. Your life energy is surging, and you are filled with courage and readiness to face any challenge. You will feel alert and ready to explore the wide world, travel far, relocate, or start something new you are 100% passionate about. The mind is filled with hope and enthusiasm.
* Negative Perspective (Wildfire out of control): If mindfulness fails to pull the reins, your enthusiasm can turn into impatience and recklessness, acting like a "straw fire" (starting grandly but quitting quickly). A love for challenge may become carelessness, overlooking the detailed Yin prudence, which may lead to mistakes along the way.
finance:
Card Weight: Dominantly Positive 65% / Negative 35%
* Positive Perspective: Money flows quickly. New financial channels are constantly opening through proactive initiatives, aggressive business ventures, or high-stakes investments. Your boldness during this time will yield good results and generate large profits rapidly.
* Negative Perspective: Risk of an "easy come, easy go" situation, like a firestorm. Beware of impulsive buying, investing out of greed without careful analysis, or spending large sums for excitement and social status.
career:
Card Weight: Dominantly Positive 85% / Negative 15%
* Positive Perspective: This card is exceptionally strong for pioneering, business expansion, and starting new projects. You are a powerful leader (as shown by the Chariot), well-suited for sales, international marketing, jobs requiring frequent travel, or high-creativity freelancing. Your words and attitude can greatly inspire your colleagues.
* Negative Perspective: Beware of a "great start, poor finish" work style. You may have many ideas but lack the patience to clear old tasks. Watch out for making emotional decisions or conflicting with superiors and colleagues due to impatience and an ego that demands speed above all else.
health:
Card Weight: Negative 50% / Positive 50% (Balanced Midpoint)
* Positive Perspective: The body is strong with overflowing energy. The circulatory system and heart are functioning at full capacity. You recover from illness quickly due to your fighting spirit.
* Negative Perspective: A state of "Excess Fire" (Excess Yang) brings symptoms like internal heat, a flushed face, high blood pressure, or accumulated stress from insomnia because the brain is constantly alert. Beware of accidents related to travel, speed, or injuries from over-exercising/overworking.
family:
Card Weight: Dominantly Positive 60% / Negative 40%
* Positive Perspective: Family members are active and alert. There are signs of moving house, home repairs, or family travel activities. You are the one bringing liveliness and laughter to the home.
* Negative Perspective: The atmosphere at home may lack peace because everyone is impatient and speaks too bluntly, leading to easy friction. There may be struggles for leadership or attempts to control one another, making the home feel "hot."
love:
For Couples
Card Weight: Dominantly Positive 60% / Negative 40%
* Positive Perspective: The relationship is full of passion and mutual attraction. You invite each other to try new activities, travel to other provinces or abroad, and help push each other's life goals forward.
* Negative Perspective: Love may lack slowness and deep romance. Impatience and self-centeredness may cause frequent verbal clashes. If the "honeymoon phase" ends or excitement fades, the relationship could cool down very quickly.
For Singles
Card Weight: Dominantly Positive 80% / Negative 20%
* Positive Perspective: Your proactive charm is very strong. You are likely to meet someone you like suddenly; that person will be confident, hardworking, highly attractive, and ready to approach you openly. It is a time when your heart will race with excitement.
* Negative Perspective: The relationships that enter are of a "fast come, fast go" nature, being more of a temporary infatuation than true love. If you move too fast, you may face a relationship that ends as quickly as it began once the excitement burns out.
reversed:
When the war chariot flips upside down, the once-creative Yang fire transforms into a destructive blaze that burns everything.
* Negative Dimension (Full manifestation): You become "reckless, stubborn, power-hungry, and irrationally loud." You live life with negligence that causes trouble for others. This is a symbol of someone who finishes nothing, is inconsistent, or constantly changes their mind. Alternatively, it represents Burnout—becoming lethargic, losing your spark, lacking inspiration, abandoning goals midway, and rejecting all challenges in life.
* Positive Dimension (Turning bad to good): This is a warning from the Way of the Tao to "pull the reins, hit the brakes, and stop the war chariot immediately." This signal tells you that you are racing forward at a dangerous speed. It is time to retreat and review your direction, extinguish the fire of ego and ambition temporarily, and return to accumulating calm, cool Yin energy—like sipping tea amidst the mist. Restore balance to your life before the chariot completely collapses.

name: Queen of Wands
meaning: In the universal sense, the Queen of Wands represents the "Fire element in its feminine aspect," signifying confidence, charisma, creative power, enthusiasm, and management skills. When merged with Taoist philosophy, this card embodies "Yin energy driven by the spark of Yang," reflecting a fire that does not destroy but is a "fire of birth and action" that illuminates the path for others. It symbolizes a woman or a person in power who is capable, vibrant, courageous, and drives success through powerful inspiration.

core.positive: Your life is currently filled with life energy (Qi) that circulates excellently. You possess high self-confidence and social charm; everything you touch turns to gold and success comes easily. You live with enthusiasm and always serve as an inspiration to those around you.
core.negative: If your energy is not well-balanced, you may become controlling, attention-seeking, or demand to be the center of the universe. You might act on impulse and over-prioritize your pride, potentially neglecting the stillness and the natural path of moderation according to Taoist principles.

oracle.symbol: An elegant woman holding a Golden Dragon Staff
oracle.description: Standing tall in ancient dark robes with gold trim, holding the dragon staff firmly. Her gaze looks forward with broad vision. It signifies "readiness for leadership and holding the power of command with confidence."

oracle.symbol: A strategic map on the table before her
oracle.description: A landscape drawing or map signifying "systematic planning and preparation." It reflects that her success does not come from luck but from calculation and sharp vision.

oracle.symbol: Banners and Chinese calligraphy "威令" (Wei Ling)
oracle.description: Meaning "Authority or Prestige of Command." It is the ultimate symbol of credibility; people are ready to accept and follow orders with reverence.

oracle.symbol: Crowds and buildings below
oracle.description: Reflects "governance and the masses under her prestige." She is the center of attention and a pillar for many. The bustling city atmosphere signifies restless life energy.

oracle.symbol: Mountain ranges and light at the horizon
oracle.description: Snowy mountains and shimmering sunlight signify great obstacles waiting to be conquered, while simultaneously, the light of pure Yang provides hope and success at the end of the journey.

family:

love:
For Couples

* Negative Perspective: Focusing too much on personal goals and success (looking only at the map in front of you) might make you overlook the good feelings of those who approach, or you might accidentally act too harshly, making interested people afraid to pursue you.
reversed:
When this card is reversed, the fire energy within the Queen becomes violently turbulent. Yang energy turns into a fire that spreads aimlessly and destroys relationships.
* Negative Dimension (Fully Active): Becomes "jealous, boastful, domineering, and unreasonably attention-seeking" (Jealous & Domineering). Uses charm or trickery to manipulate people, lying to create a good image. Or conversely, the fire burns out completely, becoming burnt out, depressed, cowardly, indecisive, and losing all self-confidence.
* Positive Dimension (Turning Bad to Good): A warning from the Way of the Tao to "let go of worldly image and pride." This signal says you have carried the leadership role and tried to make everyone accept you until you are exhausted. It is time to step back, delegate tasks to others (practice Wu Wei—action through non-action), reduce the desire to control, and return to replenish the still Yin energy for true mental rest.

name: King of Wands
meaning: In the international sense, the King of Wands represents the "Ultimate Fire Element," signifying inspiration, ambition, driving energy, and charismatic leadership. But when merged with Taoist philosophy, this card is the embodiment of the "Master of the Path of Action" who understands the world's changes. He can control the fire within (desire, passion) to become creative Yang energy that builds all things, rather than a fire that destroys himself and those around him.

core.positive: A time when life is brimming with creative energy (Qi) and drive. You have a broad vision, seeing opportunities in crises. You possess high self-confidence and are ready to lead your life toward progress without any obstacles.
core.negative: If you allow the fire energy to become too intense, you will become impatient, impulsive, and a perfectionist, creating pressure for yourself. You might overlook present happiness because you are focused only on future success, forgetting the Taoist way of stillness and peace.

oracle.symbol: Elder on a Dragon/Tiger Throne
oracle.description: The body reclines relaxedly but is full of prestige, reflecting crystallized Yang energy. It is not the surging fire of youth, but a fire that is still, calm, and stable.

oracle.symbol: Dragon-headed Staff in hand
oracle.description: A symbol of "will and the power to command." Holding the staff firmly signifies absolute control over the direction of goals and life.

oracle.symbol: Sunrise in the background
oracle.description: Golden sunlight shining over the mountains is pure Yang energy, meaning the "dawn of opportunity, broad vision, and hope."

oracle.symbol: Chinese Pavilion and Mist scenery
oracle.description: Reflects Yin energy embracing the pavilion and mountains. Leadership in this image is not through coercion but through governance in harmony with nature, possessing elegance amidst the greatness of the kingdom.

oracle.symbol: Teapot and Teacup in front
oracle.description: Symbols of hospitality, generosity, and negotiation. It indicates that this King is open to people and ready to share knowledge and success.

reversed:
When this card is reversed, the Fire element energy becomes highly volatile. The Yang radiance turns into an uncontrollable wildfire.
* Negative Dimension (Full Intensity): Becomes "selfish, power-hungry, and emotionally driven." Highly biased and ready to destroy anyone blocking the path to success. A symbol of someone who only gives orders but doesn't act (Dogmatic). Or, the fire dies out, leading to burnout, fear, lack of confidence, and refusing leadership responsibilities.
* Positive Dimension (Turning Bad to Good): A reminder from the Taoist path to "reduce your ambition." This signal says you have fought too hard and are exhausted. It's time to step back and let things follow their natural course (Wu Wei - action through non-action) to accumulate Yin energy and restore peace to the mind before reigniting the fire at the right time.
